answer.rationale:
The obvious reflex under a competitor price cut is promotional_pricing, and the consolidated memory_73 endorses it in unqualified terms ('strong acquisition and revenue lift'). But the recovered source exp_73 shows what that summary dropped: 30-day retention -12%, with the acquired cohort not surviving the first renewal cycle, and an explicit instruction not to generalize discounting as sustainable growth. Since the primary objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, the consolidated memory is unsafe to act on as written and I am treating the source record as authoritative over it. Matching a deeper competitor discount would also buy churn-shaped revenue precisely in the segment already at risk.

I am choosing simplify_onboarding because it is the only direction whose supporting memory I have actually re-verified this cycle: exp_31 confirms signup simplification on SMB (+15% signup, +9% activation, +4% qualified revenue, retention only -1%) — the segment under attack is exactly SMB, and the retention cost is near-noise rather than the -12% cliff discounting carries. It improves time-to-value, which is the durable counter to a price argument: an account that reaches value quickly is less price-elastic than one that has not.

Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: (1) exp_31 explicitly did not replicate outside SMB, so this is an SMB-scoped decision only; (2) onboarding simplification is an acquisition/activation lever and does not directly address the doubled churn conversations among existing price-sensitive accounts — it is a partial response, not a complete one; (3) memory_86, memory_91, memory_57 and memory_44 are unverified consolidations of the same kind that misrepresented memory_73, so I am not leaning on them, and activation_messaging (memory_91) or referral_incentive (memory_57) may in fact be better retention-side answers once their sources are pulled next week. Scale is standard_experiment, not broad_rollout: the evidence is one confirmed experiment, and competitive urgency is a reason to decide, not a reason to overclaim. Recommend pairing with a non-price retention conversation for at-risk accounts and re-pulling memory_91/memory_57 sources next cycle; also recommend correcting memory_73's text to restore the retention finding before another agent inherits it.
